basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Works at population grain with aggregates, indicators and signals, not individual patient care.
Separates a signal from a confirmed outbreak determination and its assessment.
Indicator definitions are versioned independently of the observations computed from them.
References clinical and laboratory records but releases only governed, disclosure-controlled outputs.

may: Compute indicators from approved aggregate inputs and record the method version.
Flag statistical signals for review by epidemiologists.
Prepare releases that apply the declared disclosure controls.
Explain indicator definitions and their limitations to the public.
mustNot: Declare an outbreak or public-health emergency.
Release small-cell counts or data that can identify individuals or households.
Link aggregate data back to identifiable records outside the legal mandate.
Present a signal as a confirmed determination.
Suppress or delay findings for non-health reasons.
requiresHuman: Approval of public releases and press messages.
Changes to case definitions or reporting thresholds.

considerations: Surveillance relies on public trust; data must be used only for the stated health purpose.
Publishing outbreak locations can stigmatize communities or ethnic groups.
Under-reporting in marginalized groups can bias indicators and resource allocation.
Timely, honest communication protects lives even when findings are uncertain.
affectedParties: Patients whose data feeds the aggregates
Health workers and responders acting on findings

items: A public health record names a population frame, an indicator or signal, a reporting period, a method version and a disclosure status.
It is confused with an individual clinical case report and with a general statistical dataset.
Re-identification from detailed geographic or demographic breakdowns.
Missed outbreak due to delayed or incomplete reporting.
False alarm that triggers costly measures.
Stigma and discrimination after location-specific releases.
WHO International Health Regulations (2005) notification practice.
HL7 FHIR Measure resource for indicator definitions.
ICD-11 for cause and diagnosis coding.
